title: RFC 8621 §4.1.4 walk uses Option<&mut Vec> to model JS nullable array references exactly
description: walk.rs parse_structure() takes text_body and html_body as Option<&mut Vec<String>>. Setting one to None inside the recursion suppresses further pushes to that list (the 'nullify' step from the RFC algorithm). A future contributor might refactor this to use bool flags or a separate enum to 'make it clearer'. That would be wrong: the RFC 8621 §4.1.4 algorithm is specified in JavaScript pseudocode where textBody and htmlBody are nullable references that get set to null. The Option<&mut Vec> type maps that semantics directly — None means 'this list has been nullified by being inside a multipart/alternative that already found a matching part type'. Any other encoding would require careful re-derivation from the RFC pseudocode to avoid subtle body classification bugs.
